West Triangle, Quezon City http: dilg.com ph DILG OPINION No. 125 s. 2022 October 10, 2022 MS. MARIA REMEDIOS CHUA-SY Ninong Osmundo St., BF Homes Ph2, Barangay 169, Caloocan City jhingsy@yahoo.com Dear Ms. Chua-Sy: This has reference to your earlier letter seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following: I. Whether or not the DILG Memorandum No. 2019-121 is legally binding even if the DILG Opinion No. 02 s. 2020 contained a Supreme Court Ruling regarding illegally parked vehicles even inside private subdivisions, inasmuch as BF Homes Phl and 2 have already been turned over to Caloocan City; 2. Up to what extent can the Local Government Unit help when you already exhausted all legal remedies made available to you? 3. If the Barangay officials are incapable of implementing the law and local ordinances, what legal remedy can be availed? 4. Can the Homeowners Association permit anyone to claim a public road for private use? Per your representation, you filed a complaint against your neighbor, Wilven Go, regarding the two (2) six-wheeler trucks which were parked in a street inside your subdivision, which is a major thoroughfare towards Novaliches and C-5 road. You represented that you sought the help of the Local Government Unit of Caloocan and thereafter, Mr. Go was found to have been operating without the necessary permits and hence, his business was meted with a closure order. You also mentioned that he still was able to operate his business again despite the closure order, and his trucks were still parked along the street of your subdivision. You then represented that you filed a complaint before the Barangay 169, Zone 15, District I but to no avail, which led you to sought the assistance of the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) but the latter remanded the case back to the "Matlno, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Barangay. You then represented that the barangay officials did nothing and told you that they cannot do anything about the matter. Hence, the instant queries. Before dwelling to the a qualification should be made on whether or not the interior streets of subdivisions were already donated or turned-over by the subdivision owner/developer to the Local Government Unit of Caloocan City. Under Section 31 of P.D. No. 957, otherwise known as the Subdivision and Condominium Buyers' Protective Degree, as amended by PD No. 12161, it is only after donation or turn-over that these roads, alleys and sidewalks in a subdivision are considered part of the public domain and are within the jurisdiction of the said city or municipality.2 In the case of Albon Femand03, the Supreme Court ruled that ownership of the streets and sidewalks in a private subdivision belongs to the subdivision owner/developer until it is transferred or acquired by the government. In connection thereto, please be apprised that parked vehicles are covered by the DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-121 (MC). The said MC is not limited to illegal structures and constructions, rather, it encompasses reclaiming of public roads which are being used for private ends.4 Let it be noted that this MC pertains to road clearing operations for purposes of returning to public use, all public roads and sidewalks that have been appropriated for private use. From the foregoing, assuming that the BF Homes Phl and 2 were indeed turned-over to the LGU of Caloocan City, then the parked vehicles along the interior streets of subdivisions are covered by the MC and may be cleared for purposes of returning to public use. Thus, the MC is only binding if indeed the streets of BF Homes Phl and 2, specifically the streets where the trucks were parked, were turned-over to the LGU of Caloocan City since these roads are considered public roads which are being used for private ends. With regard to the second query. please be informed that this department is precluded from acting on queries which are factual and justiciable in nature. As to the Sections 60(c) and 61 of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code are instructive, viz: "SECTION 60. Grounds for Disciplinary Actions. — An elective local official may be disciplined, suspended, or removed from office on any of the following grounds: xxx Defining 'Open Space" in Residential Subdivisions Amending Section 31 of PD 957 Requiring Subdivision Owners to Provide Roads, Alleys, Sidewalks and Reserve Open Space for Parks or Recreational Use. 2 DILG Opinion no. 02 s. 2020, dated 07 Janua,y 2020 G.R. No. 148357, 30 June 2006 oting White Plains Association V. court of Appeals Supra at 2 Page 2 Of 4

(c) Dishonesty, oppression, dereliction of duty; Xxx misconduct in office, gross neqliqence. or An elective local official may be removed from office on the grounds enumerated above by order of the proper court. SECTION 61. Fonn and Filing of Administrative Complaints. — A verified complaint against any erring local elective official shall be prepared as follows: (a) A complaint against any elective official of a province, a highly urbanized city, an independent component city or component city shall be filed before the Office of the President; (b) A complaint against any elective official of a municipality shall be filed before the sangguniang panlalawigan whose decision may be appealed to the Office of the President; and (c) A complaint against any elective baranqay official shall be filed before the sanqquniang panlunqsod or sanqquniang bayan concerned whose decision shall be final and executory." (Emphasis and underlining ours) From the above-cited provision, you may file a complaint against erring elective barangay officials before the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Caloocan for neglect in the performance of duty or for failure to give proper attention to a required task or to discharge a duty. Further, you may avail the legal remedy under Section 16(b)(2) and Section 18 of R.A. NO. 11201, otherwise known as the "Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development Act", thus: "Sec. 16. Jurisdiction of Regional Adjudicators. — The Regional Adjudicators shall exercise original and exclusive jurisdiction to hear and decide cases involving the following: Xxxx (b) Cases involving Homeowners Associations: Xxxx (2) Intra-association disputes or controversies arising out of the relations between and among members of HOAs; between any or all of them and the HOA of which they are members; Xxx (d) Disputes or controversies involving laws and regulations being implemented by the Department except those cases falling within the jurisdiction of other judicial or quasi-judicial body. Sec. 18. Appeals. — Decisions, awards or orders of the Regional Adjudicators shall be final and executory unless appealed to the Commission within fifteen Page 3 of 4

(15) calendar days from receipt of such decisions. awards. or orders. The decision of the Commission upon any disputed matter may be brought upon to the Court of Appeals in accordance with Rule 43 of the Rules of Court." As to the we reiterate that a qualification should be made on whether or not the interior streets of subdivisions were already donated or turned over by the subdivision owner/developer to the Local Government Unit of Caloocan. Consequently. the Homeowners Association cannot permit anyone to claim a public road for private use if indeed these internal streets of the BF Homes Phl and 2 subdivision are considered public roads and are within the jurisdiction of the City of Caloocan. Accordingly, if these roads, streets, and alleys were already donated to the LGU concerned, the parked vehicles along the interior streets of subdivisions are also covered by the said MC. What the Homeowners Association can do is only to regulate access to, or passage through the subdivision/village roads for purposes of preserving privacy, tranquility. internal security, and safety and traffic order.5 It is the right of the homeowners who invested savings in exchange for special amenities, comfort, and tighter security.ö The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY T RITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY TOR R.
